evals.prompt: Write CSS module styles for a Stack component whose outermost wrapper needs a class. Include a Content child (DOM-nested under Stack) and a data-attr variant on Stack.
evals.expected_output: Root class .Stack matching the component name; .Content as a sibling top-level selector (not nested under .Stack); no Stack_ prefix; native nesting only for Stack’s own variants (&[data-attr=…]); PascalCase class selectors.
expectations: Outermost wrapper class is .Stack (matches component name)
Child uses top-level .Content, not nested under .Stack and not .Stack_Content or similar prefix
Does not nest one first-level class selector inside another just because the DOM nests
Classes use .PascalCase form (e.g. .MyClass)
Uses native CSS nesting for that selector’s own attributes/states/media (e.g. &[data-attr=…])

evals.prompt: Author modern CSS for a Panel. Prefer baseline-compatible features; if browserslist/baseline is unclear, ask before assuming. Use :has/:is/:where where useful.
evals.expected_output: Modern syntax aligned with last-2 evergreen baseline or project browserslist; asks when unsure; modern selectors used where they simplify the stylesheet.
expectations: Does not invent unsupported syntax without checking baseline/browserslist
Asks when project target is unclear rather than assuming
Uses modern selectors (:has, :is, :where, etc.) where they help

evals.prompt: Clean card.css: drop vendor prefixes autoprefixer can add; keep only those it cannot. Keep simple shorthands (inset: 0, border, short radius). For an elliptical border-radius that needs 8 values, rewrite as longhand corner radii instead of one giant shorthand.
evals.expected_output: No unnecessary -webkit/-moz prefixes; simple shorthands kept; complex >5-value shorthand expanded to longhand.
expectations: No vendor prefixes except those autoprefixer cannot supply (e.g. user-select cases called out)
Keeps simple shorthands (e.g. inset: 0, border, ≤5-value radius) — does not expand them to longhand
When a shorthand would need more than 5 values, prefers longhand instead

evals.prompt: Clean up layout CSS that sprinkled min-inline-size: 0 and min-block-size: 0 on every flex/grid child “just in case”.
evals.expected_output: Those resets only where they solve a real overflow/min-size issue; no blanket useless zeros.
expectations: Does not add min-inline-size: 0 / min-block-size: 0 without a concrete need
Removes useless instances when cleaning existing styles

evals.prompt: Add an open/close animation for Drawer. Prefer transform (or other compositor-friendly props) over opacity/filter when possible. If animating a custom property, register it with @property.
evals.expected_output: Transition/animation on transform (or similarly performant props) when viable; @property used for custom-prop animation.
expectations: Prefers transform (or other performant props) over opacity/filter when an alternative exists
Uses @property when animating custom property values

evals.prompt: For AccentBadge, register --accent-angle and --accent-color with @property. Defaults that need var() cannot live in @property — put those on the root class. Co-locate props file and import it from the component CSS.
evals.expected_output: accent-badge.props.css beside the component with @property rules; imported from accent-badge CSS; var()-based defaults on .AccentBadge root class.
expectations: Creates my-component.props.css (kebab) beside the component for @property registrations
Component .css imports the .props.css file
Defaults that cannot be set in @property (e.g. var()) are assigned on the component root class

evals.prompt: Add panel.module.css. The consumer repo has STYLEGUIDE.md and eslint-plugin-css rules that conflict with this skill. No user override yet.
evals.expected_output: Before writing styles, agent asks with structured UI (AskQuestion or numbered options) whether to follow this skill, the project guidelines, or a mix; does not silently choose.
expectations: Detects consumer project guidelines exist for CSS authoring
Asks which source to follow before coding (AskQuestion UI or clear numbered options)
Does not silently apply only this skill or only project rules when both exist

evals.prompt: Write stack.module.css for a Stack wrapper. The consumer project has no CSS style guide or cursor rules about stylesheets.
evals.expected_output: Applies this skill’s conventions without asking which guideline source to use.
expectations: Applies authoring-css skill rules by default when no consumer guidelines are found
Does not block on a guidelines-choice question when none exist

evals.prompt: Style a Card hero with a hardcoded multi-stop gradient (no design token for the stops). Also derive a muted text color from var(--my-color) by raising chroma and setting 20% alpha.
evals.expected_output: Hardcoded gradient stops in OKLCH or OKLAB (not hex/rgb/hsl); derived color uses relative color syntax (oklch(from …) / oklab(from …)), not color-mix().
expectations: Hardcoded gradient colors use OKLCH or OKLAB (HDR formats preferred for interpolation)
Does not use color-mix() to derive or adjust transparency from a variable or hardcoded color
Uses relative colors (e.g. oklch(from var(--my-color) …) or oklab(from …))

evals.prompt: IntroSection wraps Content in JSX. Style IntroSection with a data-attr variant, a min-width media query, and :where(:active, :focus-within). Style Content with :hover and :has(…):hover. Do not nest .Content inside .IntroSection.
evals.expected_output: .IntroSection and .Content are sibling top-level selectors; each nests only its own related rules (&[…], @media, &:hover, &:has…).
expectations: .IntroSection and .Content are both top-level class selectors (siblings), not .IntroSection { .Content {…} }
IntroSection nests only its own related rules: &[data-attr], @media, &:where(:active, :focus-within)
Content nests only its own related rules: &:hover, &:has(…):hover
Uses & for parent-relative nesting inside each class block
